article_title: Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis
citation: Jueng, Ekkachai. (2026). Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10802
title: Q-Learning Lab: a single-file bilingual browser tool for teaching tabular Q-learning
description: Q-Learning Lab is a 'single-file, browser-based, bilingual (Thai/English) tool for teaching tabular Q-learning that requires no installation and no network connection.' It renders a 5×5 gridworld with color-coded Q-values and policy arrows, exposes a live Bellman-substitution panel showing the numeric update at every step, logs every transition with the full pre-action Q-row, and exports the trace as CSV for learner-side analysis.
requirements: Runs offline from one HTML file with no external dependencies; the article states it 'runs from a double-click on any modern browser'.
constraints: Tabular Q-learning on a deterministic, fully observable, single-agent gridworld only; stochastic transitions, function approximation, continuing tasks, and multi-agent settings are 'out of scope by design'.
target_learners: undergraduates in introductory machine-learning / reinforcement-learning courses
target_learning_goals: diagnosing agent behavior against the optimal policy
key_sources: Jueng, Ekkachai. (2026). Q-Learning Lab: Teaching Reinforcement Learning Through Learner-Generated Trace Analysis. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10802

article_title: Nursing competencies for family-centred care in the hospital setting: A multinational Q-methodology study.
citation: Hengeveld B, Maaskant JM, Lindeboom R, Marshall AP, Vermeulen H, Eskes AM. (2021). Nursing competencies for family‐centred care in the hospital setting: A multinational Q‐methodology study. Journal of Advanced Nursing, 77(4), 1783–1799. https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.14719
title: Ranked Q-set of 72 nursing competencies for family-centred care in hospitals
description: A ranked set of 72 nursing competencies for family-centred care in the hospital setting, developed through an integrative review and categorized using CanMEDS key concepts, then ranked by 69 Dutch and Australian professionals via online Q-sort. The article states "Our set of competencies can be used to guide education and evaluate practicing nurses in hospitals" and considers them generalist competencies each hospital nurse should have. The set overlaps the 2017 IFNA competency set, with 23 competencies the authors identify as new or markedly different.
requirements: Competencies were derived from published literature and validated for importance with lecturers, researchers, registered nurses and policy makers; family members were not included among raters
constraints: The article notes the comparison with the IFNA set was subjective because differences in descriptions made direct comparison difficult, and that reducing the number of competencies would very likely improve usability in research and practice
target_learning_goals: Family-centred care competencies: communication, collaboration, advocacy and partnership with patients and families
examples: Participants ranked the 72 competencies on an 11-column quasi-normal Q-sort table via a web-based system, with commentaries collected on their five highest and lowest ranked items
key_sources: Hengeveld B, Maaskant JM, Lindeboom R, Marshall AP, Vermeulen H, Eskes AM. (2021). Nursing competencies for family‐centred care in the hospital setting: A multinational Q‐methodology study. Journal of Advanced Nursing, 77(4), 1783–1799. https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.14719
